description: Step 2 of the extern door collapse. Measured on 2026-09-13 with a two-crate probe (dependency rlib with an unreferenced no_mangle export in its own object file; bin looks it up with dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT)): without an export flag the export is dropped from the binary on both macOS and Linux and dlsym fails; with -Wl,-export_dynamic (macOS) or -rdynamic (Linux) the unreferenced export survives the link and dlsym finds it. So the two compiler-side name->address tables exist only because executables do not export their symbols by default; the AOT link already passes -rdynamic for the same reason (aot_link.rs). Change: the fz package build script passes the export flag for its bins and test binaries; fz_extern_symbol_addr is unchanged and now finds fz's own exports the way it finds sqrt. Deleted: runtime_symbol_addrs and the production rows of register_runtime_symbols (src/ir_codegen/backend.rs), the interpreter's name->address match and its 60-name use list (src/ir_interp/extern_call.rs), every_declared_runtime_symbol_is_reachable_from_compiled_code. Proof: nm shows fz_aot_setup present in fz2 after the flag; every_declared_runtime_symbol_resolves passes with the address book gone; full gate; Linux CI.
title: Export the compiler's symbols dynamically; delete the JIT registry and the interpreter address book
